content.text: {"headline":"Approve P1: no-cost breaks, cross-skill moves and callback keep Payments on target at zero extra cost","why":"The Payments shortfall is a capacity problem, not a demand problem. There have been 11 sick absences today against a usual 2, mostly flu. Agents on the phones fell to 24 against 28–29 planned, and service level dropped to 60.3% at 12:30. Volume is only up 6%. For the disruption window (15:00–18:45), the forecast now looks healthy even with no action: P0 predicts 97.3%, well above the 80% target. P1 nudges that to 97.5% (Payments 96.4%, General 99.1%) at no cost. It also cuts predicted abandons from 0.7% to 0.3% and lifts the rest-of-day figure to 95.0%. It does this by moving 3 cross-skilled agents to Payments 15:00–16:00, delaying 15:00–15:45 breaks by 30 minutes, moving 2 more agents 18:00–20:00 and switching on IVR callback 18:00–20:00. No policy issues; no escalation needed.","trade_offs":["P0 (no action) also meets target at 97.3% and costs nothing, but abandons stay at 0.7% versus 0.3% with P1.","P2 costs ₹759 for 97.6% (Payments 96.7%). It slightly dents General (98.9% vs 99.1%) and keeps abandons at 0.7%, so it is a marginal gain for real money.","P3 costs ₹1,440 for the best result, 97.9% (Payments 97.0%, rest of day 96.2%). That is only 0.4 points better than P1 in the window.","P1 takes 3 and then 2 agents from General, but General is still predicted at 99.1%, so risk to that queue looks low.","Delaying breaks asks more of an already short-staffed Payments team."],"watch":"Watch Payments agents on the phones and service level through 15:00–16:00 and again from 18:00. Any further flu absences could widen the gap beyond what the free levers cover. If Payments drifts toward 80%, P3's evening overtime (₹1,440) is the ready step-up. Also confirm that General holds near 99% while it lends agents."}
